chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Al-Washshāʾ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I heard him عليه السلام saying: “Beware of the belittled sins, for indeed they have one who seeks them out. One of you says: ‘I commit a sin and seek forgiveness.’”
Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “And We write what they have sent ahead and their آثار, and We have enumerated every thing in a manifest Imam.”

And He, Mighty and Majestic, said: “Indeed, if it be the weight of a mustard seed, and it be in a rock, or in the heavens, or in the earth, Allah will bring it forth. Indeed Allah is Subtle, All-Aware.”

key_terms.آثَارَهُمْ: their traces, effects, or lasting consequences
key_terms.إِمَامٍ مُبِينٍ: a manifest Imam; a clear comprehensive register
key_terms.الْمُحَقَّرَاتِ: sins regarded as trivial or insignificant
key_terms.خَبِيرٌ: fully aware of all realities and details
key_terms.طَالِبًا: one who pursues, seeks out, or calls to account
key_terms.مِثْقَالَ حَبَّةٍ: the weight of a single grain
key_terms.نَكْتُبُ: We record and write down deeds

ai.seo_question: Why does Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام warn against small sins in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith warns against treating small sins as insignificant, because every deed is recorded and brought forth by Allah. By citing Qur’anic verses, it emphasizes divine knowledge, precise reckoning, and the certainty that even the smallest act will not escape accountability.
